text:
incident-bot: Pager alert: sustained 5xx spike on /v1/chat/stream from model-runner-prod across eu-central-1. 5xx = 14.6% in last 4m (baseline 0.4%). Auto-paging oncall. Runbook: https://redwood/runbooks/model-runtime-5xx

oncall-maya: Acknowledged, I'm on pager. Any recent infra/deploys?

jin (eng-runtime): There was an automated image promotion 22m ago with commit c4a9e2 that included a new fused-attn kernel and a GPU memory optimizer. Canary looked fine but maybe a different workload hit it.

rachel (sre): Alert details: error classes include SIGSEGV and GPU memory allocation failures. Pods show repeated restarts; kubectl describe shows OOMKilled and CrashLoopBackOff.

oncall-maya: First step: enable safe-mode routing—send all traffic to model-variant:stable-64 to avoid the new optimized kernel. Flipping now.

ops-bot: Routing set: 100% -> model-variant:stable-64.

sam (ml-infra): Pulling logs from affected pod model-runner-eu-0: last lines show GPU MMAP failed followed by segfault inside libfused_attn.so: 
```
E 09:07:12.502 model-runner[3112]: gpu error: cuMemAlloc failed: out of memory
E 09:07:12.503 model-runner[3112]: backtrace:
  0x7f8b1a1a libfused_attn.so(+0x6b2a)
  0x7f8b1a9f ModelRunner::compute()
  0x55c1d0 serve_request
```
Also saw a metadata tag: seq_len=2048 on some large evals.

jin (eng-runtime): That commit introduced a new allocation strategy that aggressively preallocates workspace for long sequence lengths. Looks like certain eval workloads with seq_len=2048 trigger huge allocations and race to OOM. I can roll that change back.

oncall-maya: While jin prepares rollback, let's reduce concurrency and max_concurrent_requests on frontend routers to avoid bursting memory. Set max_concurrent_requests for model-runner service to 8 (was 64).

ops-bot: Frontend config updated: max_concurrent_requests=8.

kai (eng-oncall-2nd): Also recommend disabling autoscale up to avoid spinning new pods that immediately crash. I'll set HPA max to current replica count (6).

rachel (sre): Doing controlled drain and restart of crashing pods after router change. Monitoring. 5xx down to 5.2% in 3m.

sam (ml-infra): I fetched a core dump and GPU debug trace: `/var/crash/core.eucrunner.3112` and `nvidia-smi pmon` logs show memory exhaustion prior to segfault. I'll upload artifacts: s3://redwood-incidents/1840056789/cores/ and share link shortly.

jin (eng-runtime): Rolling back commit c4a9e2 now. New image tag: `gcr.io/redwood/model-runner:rollback-c4a9e2-184005`. Deploying to canary subset.

oncall-maya: Canary with rollback looks stable so far. No segfaults in the last 6m on canary. Gradual rollout to remaining pods.

ops-bot: Routing remains to stable variant. Alert update: 5xx rate 1.8% (was 14.6%). Severity lowered to P2.

rachel (sre): Customer impact: quick query for affected customers: `select customer_id, count(*) from requests where status>=500 and ts>now()-interval '15 minutes' group by customer_id order by count desc limit 20;` Top hits: cust-scout (980), cust-nimbus (145), perf-eval (90).

oncall-maya: cust-scout traffic appears routed through eu-central-1 where the failures concentrated. Can we route cust-scout to dedicated-reserved pool dw-eu-03 temporarily?

kai (eng-oncall-2nd): I can move cust-scout. Switching now.

ops-bot: routing update: cust-scout -> dw-eu-03.

sam (ml-infra): Core dump analysis preliminary: failure path is allocation for attention workspace when seq_len>1024 combined with prealloc enabled. There's a null-check missing when fallback allocation fails, leading to deref of null pointer in fused kernel. I'll open a bug with attached core.

jin (eng-runtime): Pushing a hotfix to add graceful fallback when workspace allocation fails and to disable prealloc by default. Hotfix image: `gcr.io/redwood/model-runner:hotfix-prealloc-184005`. Rolling out now.

rachel (sre): Hotfix rollout complete across cluster. No new 5xx in last 10m. Current 5xx 0.6%.

oncall-maya: Preparing customer notifications: cust-scout support ping, and status page incident created?

ops-bot: Incident created: https://status.redwood/incident/RE-1840056789.

sam (ml-infra): Uploaded cores and traces: s3://redwood-incidents/1840056789/ and linked to ticket INC-1840056789.

jin (eng-runtime): Tests to add: workload tests with seq_len 0, 128, 512, 1024, 2048 and low-memory GPU environments. Also adding guard for null workspace pointer. PRs: https://git.redwood/p/r/3501 (rollback), https://git.redwood/p/r/3502 (prealloc guard).

rachel (sre): Handoff: I'll hand to Kai for 2hr watch. Summary note for postmortem: cause = aggressive preallocation and a missing null-check in fused attention kernel triggered OOM and segfaults under long-seq eval jobs. Mitigations: routing to stable variant, reduce frontend concurrency, pin HPA, rollback commit, hotfix to disable prealloc and add guard, move high-impact customer to dedicated pool. Affected customers: cust-scout (mitigated), cust-nimbus (minor), perf-eval.

oncall-maya: Action items recorded:
- Jin: roll back and hotfix PRs referenced (3501, 3502)
- Sam: collect GPU traces and upload artifacts (done)
- Rachel: draft incident summary and update status page
- Kai: 2hr watch then handoff, coordinate postmortem doc

kai (eng-oncall-2nd): Taking watch. No further action unless alerts spike. Thanks all :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Handoff entry added: oncall -> kai at 1840057140.

rachel (sre): Marking incident resolved candidate: sustained <1% 5xx for 6m. Will follow up with postmortem.

oncall-maya: Leaving note: detection 1840056789, routing -> 1840056840, rollback initiated -> 1840057000, hotfix rolled -> 1840057220. If anything else pops, tag this thread.

kai (eng-oncall-2nd): Acknowledged.

ops-bot: Incident archived as mitigated P2. Postmortem required.
